steps.en: Ejection fraction by the biplane disks method is the reference measure of left ventricular systolic function. You trace the endocardial border in the apical four chamber and apical two chamber views at end diastole and end systole, the machine stacks twenty disks along the long axis of each trace, and ejection fraction is the stroke volume divided by the end diastolic volume. The whole result stands or falls on two skills: finding a true apex without foreshortening, and tracing compact myocardium rather than trabeculation.
Record the apical four chamber, then tilt forward to the apical two chamber, keeping the apex at the top of the sector and the cavity at its longest in both.
Freeze end diastole on the frame with the largest cavity, just after mitral closure at the onset of the QRS.
Trace from one mitral annulus corner around the apex to the other corner, hugging compact myocardium and leaving trabeculation inside the cavity.
Freeze end systole on the frame with the smallest cavity, just before aortic closure, and trace again in both views.
Check that the two long axis lengths differ by less than ten percent; if not, one view is foreshortened and you must reacquire it.
Index both volumes to body surface area before judging them against the reference ranges.
Foreshortened apex cutting off the true tip. Fix: Slide apically and angle the probe until the cavity length stops growing. A rounded short apex overreads ejection fraction.
Tracing around trabeculation instead of compact wall. Fix: Trace the compact wall and leave the trabecular mesh inside the blood pool, the same way in both views.
Picking the wrong frames for diastole and systole. Fix: End diastole is the largest cavity and end systole the smallest, timed against the ECG, not guessed from wall motion.
Recording volumes when the border is not seen. Fix: Gain down until the blood pool is dark and the wall is bright; use contrast when two or more segments still drop out.
Left ventricular ejection fraction. 52 percent or more in men, 54 percent or more in women. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification, section on left ventricular volumes and ejection fraction
End diastolic volume indexed to body surface area. 34 to 74 ml per sq m in men, 29 to 61 ml per sq m in women. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification, section on left ventricular volumes
End systolic volume indexed to body surface area. 11 to 31 ml per sq m in men, 8 to 24 ml per sq m in women. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification, section on left ventricular volumes
Absolute end diastolic volume. 62 to 150 ml in men, 46 to 106 ml in women. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification, section on left ventricular volumes
A regional wall motion defect after infarction makes a single plane misleading, so both planes and the wall map matter.
Irregular rhythm needs several beats averaged rather than one convenient beat.
A dyssynchronous ventricle changes shape through systole, so the smallest cavity frame is the anchor, not the ECG alone.

q.en: Which frame is end diastole for a volume trace?

o.en: The largest cavity, just after mitral closure at QRS onset
The smallest cavity, just before aortic closure
The frame where the aortic valve first opens
Any mid systolic frame with a sharp border

why.en: End diastole is the frame of largest volume, just after mitral valve closure at the onset of the QRS.

o.en: Around the outside of the trabeculation
Midway through the wall
Along compact myocardium, leaving trabeculation inside
Along the epicardium for extra margin

why.en: The blood tissue interface for volumes is the compact endocardium. Tracing around trabeculation shrinks the cavity and overreads ejection fraction.

q.en: Which ejection fraction counts as abnormal?

o.en: Below 40 percent in men
Below 45 percent in women
Below 50 percent in either sex
Below 52 percent in men and below 54 percent in women

why.en: The ASE 2015 lower reference limits are 52 percent in men and 54 percent in women.

q.en: How do you check the two views agree before trusting the result?

o.en: Average the two volumes and judge the mean
Check the two long axis lengths differ by under ten percent
Pick the sharper border and discard the other
Trace a third view and keep any two

why.en: Matched long axis lengths prove neither view is foreshortened. A length mismatch above ten percent means reacquire, not average.

q.en: Which indexed end diastolic volume is read correctly?

o.en: 34 ml per sq m or less in men is normal
74 ml per sq m in men is clearly dilated
29 ml per sq m in women is dilated
61 ml per sq m in women is normal

why.en: The male reference range is 34 to 74 and the female range 29 to 61 ml per sq m, so 61 in a woman sits at the upper limit while 74 in a man is the top of normal.
